## Overview

Aronszajn taught in the Department of Mathematics at the University of Kansas from 1951-1977. This collection contains correspondence, notes, and publications.

## Dates

  * Creation: 1951 - 1977

## Creator

  * Aronszajn, Nachman, 1907- (Person)

## Conditions Governing Access

These materials are stored in the KU Annex off-site storage area.
All researchers interested in reviewing this material must consult Spencer Research Library Public Services staff (785-864-4334 or ksrlref@ku.edu, 9-5 M-F CST) no less than three days in advance of a planned visit. Be advised that drop-in requests for this material cannot be accommodated.

## Conditions Governing Use

Spencer Library staff may determine use restrictions dependent on the physical condition of manuscript materials.

## Biography of Nachman Aronszajin

Aronszajn received his Ph.D. in Poland in 1930. He joined the faculty of KU in 1951, becoming a Summerfield Distinguished Scholar in 1964. He retired in 1977 and died in 1980.

# Présentation

Ce site contient les archives mathématiques d’Alexandre Grothendieck de 1949 à 1991. On y trouvera des manuscrits, des « tapuscrits », parfois des documents imprimés, dans un classement fidèle pour l’essentiel (quand il existait ) au classement de l’auteur. Sur les 28000 (environ) pages de ce fonds, seules 18000 (environ) sont actuellement accessibles : pour des raisons de droits on ne peut diffuser les lettres des correspondants de Grothendieck sans leur autorisation.

#### Notice bibliographique

Alexandre Grothendieck (1928-2014) est considéré par ses pairs comme l’un des plus grands mathématiciens du XXème siècle. Son apport fondamental réside dans la refonte de la géométrie algébrique.

Son père, Alexander Schapiro (dit Sascha), né en Ukraine d’une famille juive, est anarchiste.

In 1970, he found his answer. Upon learning that the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques, where he was then working, received grants from the Ministry of Defense, Grothendieck resigned.
Since then, however, the master has never stopped writing, corresponding, or working. In 1990, he entrusted his entire mathematical archive to Jean Malgoire. This former student, a Professor r at the University of Montpellier, kept the Grothendieck archives at his home until 2010, when he deposited them at the University of Montpellier.

## Unpublished Manuscripts

The Grothendieck collection comprises unpublished manuscripts on major mathematical theories of the 20th century, particularly in algebraic geometry. It represents the majority of Grothendieck’s work from 1949 to 1991 and reveals the scholarly exchanges of a mathematician at the pinnacle of international research. It also provides insights into the development of his body of work.
After inventory and conservation measures, these documents were digitized beginning in 2016. Since May 10, a significant portion of them (approximately 18,000 pages) has been freely available online. What can we discover there? Undoubtedly, new flashes of genius, scattered throughout his numerous and diverse writings.“Seeds that it will be up to us to bring to fruition,”suggests Jean Malgoire. In the realm of mathematics, Alexandre Grothendieck may not yet have finished shedding light on uncharted territories.

# Some of Grothendieck’s archives published online by the University of Montpellier

Alexandre Grothendieck is considered one of the greatest mathematicians of the 20th century. He revolutionised the foundations and the mathods of algebraic geometry. A Fields medal winner in 1966, he was a permanent professor at IHES from 1959 to 1970, and in 1973 he joined the University of Montpellier. The latter just published an important fraction of the Grothendieck’s archives, 18000 pages out of 28000.

The archives consist of some of Alexandre Grothendieck’s handwritten and typed notes, as well as of some of his letters. It contains his works for the period 1949 – 1991 and some so far unpublished manuscripts.

Alexandre Grothendieck himself gave the documents to Jean Malgoire, one of his former students working as a researcher and professor at the University of Montpellier, in two times: once in 1990 and once in 1995. Jean Malgoire kept Grothedieck’s archives until 2010, when he gave them to the University of Montpellier, which took charge of their digitalisation and online publication.

You can find them at the following address: grothendieck.umontpellier.fr.

# Publication of the CSG website

  * 20 November 2024

The Grothendieck Institute is glad to announce the publication of the website of the Centre for Grothendieckian Studies (CSG):

As an institutional repository and online platform for materials relating to Alexander Grothendieck, the CSG website represents a comprehensive resource for anyone interested in Grothendieck’s life and work, comprising catalogues of his published and unpublished works, references to the secondary literature, transcriptions, news about ongoing research projects and events, and much more.

Through this widespread engagement, the Centre for Grothendieckian Studies strives to expand the accessibility of Grothendieck’s extraordinary scientific and cultural heritage to experts and the general public, while disseminating his revolutionary ideas.

#### The BnF archive

A collection of unpublished manuscripts by A. Grothendieck has been integrated into the National Library of France collections. Bequeathed by Grothendieck to the Library, this collection is complemented by a donation from his children. It consists, on one hand, of a corrected typescript of La Clef des Songes, and on the other hand, of a handwritten work titled Réflexions sur la Vie et le Cosmos, spanning across 41 volumes and composed of Géométrie élémentaire schématique (1992), Structures de la Psyché, developed from 1992 to 1993, Équations de Maxwell (1992-1994), and Le Problème du Mal, a work composed between 1993 and 1997, of almost 15,000 pages. This collection, of major importance for research, joins the Manuscripts department of the BnF alongside those of other eminent scientists.

Since September 2023, access to this archive, known under the name of Fonds Alexandre Grothendieck, has been possible but restricted to in-person visits by researchers. You can consult it at the Richelieu Library – Manuscripts Reading Room.

# Published Works

> Le rôle de l’écriture n’est pas de consigner les résultats d’une recherche, mais bien le processus même de la recherche.
> 
> Récoltes et Semailles, A. Grothendieck

Addressing A. Grothendieck’s extensive body of published works involves key considerations. Initially, while Grothendieck’s mathematical and literary reflections spanned his entire life, it was only the active period from 1950 to 1969 that saw traditional forms of regular publication. Post this phase, publishing his works became sporadic and complex. Additionally, at present, a wealth of unpublished material holds potential for posthumous publication. With these aspects in focus, the CSG is committed to enhancing accessibility and collaborating with publishing houses to effectively study, catalog and enlarge A. Grothendieck’s body of published works. This endeavor aims to formally categorize and grant citability to all of Grothendieck’s publications in a unified fashion.

While more sophisticated readers who are familiar with Grothendieck’s main contributions will be most interested in the unpublished works, even within the realm of these published works, their classifications, and posthumous additions, these experts might come across novel or less familiar items.

## Rights and access

Grothendieck's writings are in copyright, held by his heirs; the 2024 Hartshorne edition thanks Johanna Grothendieck and her brothers for permission to publish⁠[22]. In a declaration dated 3 January 2010 he called illicit any edition of his texts made without his agreement, in the past or during his lifetime, and asked libraries to withdraw such books⁠[7].

The Montpellier scans are free to read, but the university's legal notice reserves all reproduction rights, downloadable documents included⁠[30]. The department therefore keeps no copy of them; it holds a manifest of every file, with links. The BnF fonds is consulted only on request to the Manuscripts department, which serves a digitised copy first. The digitised volumes are on Gallica intramuros, viewable only on the library's own workstations; the originals are shown only on a justified request⁠[31]⁠[16]⁠[24].

### Centre for Grothendieckian Studies

The Centre for Grothendieckian Studies (CSG) is a research centre of the Grothendieck Institute,  with a dedicated mission to honour the memory of Alexander Grothendieck, an influential mathematician, thinker and writer of the 20th century. Through extensive efforts, we strive to enlarge the accessibility of his remarkable scientific and cultural heritage to experts and the general public while disseminating his groundbreaking ideas.

The CSG offers a valuable online resource featuring extensive surveys and catalogues of Grothendieck’s works as well as of modern Grothendieckian scholarship. This dynamic database provides summaries and digital access to a wide range of materials, including catalogues, unpublished works, bibliographic references, editorial projects, transcriptions, ongoing research, events, and much more. Explore our vibrant community, and get in touch!

As an institutional repository and online platform for materials relating to Alexander Grothendieck, the CSG’s website represents an international point of reference for Grothendieckian studies.

### DescriptionBookmark this section

In this dissertation we prove some results about the existence of families of Aronszajn trees on successors of regular cardinals which are pairwise not club isomorphic. The history of this topic begins with a theorem of Gaifman and Specker in the 1960s which asserts the existence from ZFC of many pairwise not isomorphic Aronszajn trees. Since that result was proven, the focus has turned to comparing Aronszajn trees with respect to isomorphisms on a club of levels, instead of on the entire tree.
